title: The Net Comes First

lines.text: Alaska might hold thirty thousand kinds of insect.
It has names for about nine thousand.
The strange part isn't the gap. Somebody already built a machine to close it.
Derek Sikes runs the insect collection at Alaska's Museum of the North.
Since two thousand six its catalog went from one thousand entries to four hundred thousand.
Those entries cover about two million pinned insects, each logged the day it arrives.
Sequence one, and if it matches nothing in the world's databases, you might be holding something new.
The Anchorage Daily News profiled him this week. This part wasn't in it.
In two thousand eight, a study taught a neural network to name species from a gene.
Ninety seven point five percent, on eighty unknown ground beetles.
That's the machine. One of its four authors was Derek Sikes.
Eighteen years on, Alaska's list grows about a thousand species a decade.
Twenty one thousand unnamed, at a thousand a decade. Two hundred ten years.
So the model was never what was holding this up.
A classifier needs a D N A sequence. A sequence needs a specimen.
And a specimen needs somebody in a field with a net.
Maybe a newer model moves that. Nobody's tested one here.
Those two million insects are what any method has to read first.
So what should Alaska buy. A smarter model, or another summer in the field?

deliberate_losses: the Sweden 1,000-in-the-1700s starting figure (kept only the 30,000 total and the century)
the museum's own 425,000-records-as-of-January-2026 refinement (ADN's 'more than 400,000' is the spoken figure, the precise number sits in the claims file)
the skipper-butterfly accuracy figures from the 2008 abstract (95.63, 96.10 and 100 percent), cut because one accuracy number lands and four become a table
the Sweden comparison in full, cut at Gate 0E round 2 for failing the cold read twice
gate_0e_fixes: line 6/7 said 'paper' twice in adjacent lines for a NEWSPAPER and an ACADEMIC PAPER; the cold reader backtracked. Now 'a newspaper' and 'a study'.
records vs specimens were indistinguishable by ear, which is the exact unit conflation claims.json forbids. Now 'catalog entries' and 'pinned insects'.
the 210-year figure arrived without its derivation. The arithmetic is now audible: 'at a thousand a decade'.
the Sweden line had no stated connection to the argument. It now says what it is for: less ground, later start.

ROUND 2: 'the shortcut' was an undefined abstraction the listener carried for seven lines and the payoff was never stated outright. The plant is now a concrete object ('somebody already built a machine to close it') and line 9 names the payoff ('That's the machine').

ROUND 2: the Sweden comparison was CUT as a whole fact. Two cold reads in a row could not place it in the argument and it failed the swap test against the fair-counter line. Trimming a whole fact is the correct move over trimming connective tissue.
ROUND 2: the newspaper is now named (Anchorage Daily News), so the reference is checkable.
ROUND 2: the entries-to-insects relationship is now stated rather than left for the listener to infer ('Those entries cover about two million pinned insects').

ROUND 3: restored the DNA-sequencing mechanism as a new line 6. The first synth came in at 79.3s against an 84 to 96s band, and this was the most valuable thing the earlier trim had thrown away: it establishes what a SEQUENCE is before line 14 says a classifier needs one.
